events.title: Romanian Salt Springs
events.description: People living in what is now Romania boiled water from natural salt springs to collect salt. This is one of the oldest known salt-making sites in the world.

events.title: Solnitsata Salt Center
events.description: At Solnitsata in present-day Bulgaria, people produced salt by boiling brine. The settlement later became one of Europe's earliest known towns.

events.title: Salt in Egyptian Tombs
events.description: Ancient Egyptians placed salt, salted birds and fish inside tombs as valuable funeral offerings.

events.title: Egyptian Salt Trade
events.description: Egypt exported salted fish to the Phoenicians in exchange for cedar wood, glass and the famous Tyrian purple dye.

events.title: All Your Base Are Belong to Us
events.description: A poorly translated cutscene from the game Zero Wing spreads across the early internet, becoming one of the first major viral memes.

events.title: Rickrolling Takes Off
events.description: The bait-and-switch prank of linking to Rick Astley’s ‘Never Gonna Give You Up’ becomes a massive internet phenomenon.

events.title: Doge Meme Rises
events.description: The Shiba Inu photo paired with broken English captions like ‘such wow’ and ‘very meme’ explodes in popularity.

events.title: Distracted Boyfriend Goes Viral
events.description: A stock photo of a man checking out another woman while walking with his girlfriend becomes one of the most widely used meme templates.
